newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan gives first licence for CT-2 telecom mode.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan gives first licence for CT-2 telecom mode.

text.p: Taiwan's Ministry of Transportation and Communications granted on Monday the first licence to a private firm to operate the Second Generation Cordless Telephone (CT-2) business on the island.
"We have granted a licence to Best Way Communication Company to operate the CT-2 business in (central) Taichung," a ministry official said by telephone.
"Eight more companies are waiting for approval," he said, adding that additional licences would be issued within days.
The CT-2 system covers shorter distances than regular cellular phones can cover. The CT-2 telephones can receive signals within 200 metres from each cell base.
In 1995 Taiwan permitted nine private companies to build bases for the CT-2 business as part of its effort to open up the state-controlled telecommunication industry to private interests.
In early August, South Korea's state-backed Korea Telecom signed a contract to buy 20 percent of a T$3 billion project by Taiwan's Pacific Wire and Cable to operate the CT-2 business in Taiwan.
The Pacific project would build 200,000 cell sites across Taiwan and is expected to have 100,000 users by the end of 1996, a Pacific official said.
